name: Anthemis nobilis extract
description: Anthemis nobilis extract (CAS 84649-86-5 ), derived from Roman chamomile flowers, is a botanical ingredient used across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food applications for its recognized flavoring and fragrance profile. Known under FEMA 2274 , it is a commercially established extract sought by formulators requiring a natural chamomile source with documented identity. Procurement typically targets this material for its botanical origin. In flavor formulations, it contributes a warm, apple-like floral character to beverages, confectionery, and herbal food products where natural chamomile flavor is specified. Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrances. It is also used in functional fragrances and personal care products where soft floral botanical notes are required. Cosmetic formulators use it in rinse-off and leave-on products like shampoos, toners, and creams. In these applications, a chamomile-sourced botanical extract supports natural labeling claims. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers source it for oral preparations and herbal product lines where Roman chamomile is a declared ingredient. Anthemis nobilis extract is supplied as a liquid extract or dry powder, depending on the solvent system and concentration used in production. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications. These grades are aligned with FEMA and IFRA guidelines. Buyers should confirm extraction solvent, standardization parameters, and country of botanical origin when evaluating suppliers for their specific manufacturing needs.
